brief.analystNote: BTC at $79,941 sits in a structurally compelling position — 97% through Phase B with the Phase C trigger at $80,216 only 0.34% away — but today's data mosaic does not yet justify an aggressive add. The critical gap is ETF velocity: +$175M on Sep 4 is directionally correct but falls 34% below the $264M/day baseline and is less than half the $500M/day threshold mandated for Phase B→C confirmation; without institutional ETF firepower, the breakout lacks the demand-side structure to hold $80,216 as support. LTH net position at -15,853 BTC/day (-0.377% of liquid supply) represents the single most concerning on-chain signal — this magnitude of long-term holder distribution, if sustained, historically creates overhead supply capable of capping a breakout and prolonging consolidation. On the positive side, MVRV at 1.18 (fair value), DXY weakness at 98.74, and Trump's White House Crypto Clarity Act push provide a constructive medium-term backdrop that aligns with the firm's 1-2 year horizon. The market regime note flags insufficient history for full anchor derivation (only 1 cycle of data against 120+ required thresholds) — while anchors are derived from realized price and SMA200 and remain operationally valid, the Phase system's statistical confidence will strengthen materially as more cycles accumulate. Hold current positions and await a confirmed daily close above $80,216 with ETF flows exceeding $500M before executing any Phase C allocation.
brief.riskWarning: A second macro shock — particularly a hotter-than-expected CPI print or hawkish FOMC surprise — could trigger another liquidity cascade similar to Sep 4's $200B liquidation event, breaking BTC below the $77,230 (20d SMA) and potentially retesting $69,753 (200d SMA Phase A/B line), invalidating the Phase B breakout thesis entirely.
